facts.text: Woodbine earned its name from the dense growth of the woodbine plant that once covered the original town site.
The town was platted in 1866, the same year the Chicago Northwestern Railroad began regular service through the area.
Woodbine’s downtown Brick Street Historic District, along with the Lincolnway and Carnegie Library, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Zell Millard Historic Preservation Park showcases the original depot, a CNW caboose, and a 1928 canopy gas station now serving as the town’s welcome center.
Woodbine sits along the Boyer River in Harrison County, Iowa, giving the town a scenic riverside setting.
Woodbine officially incorporated as a town in 1877, solidifying its community structure after a decade of growth.
